The drug-delivery MD literature on polyanhydrides that does exist appears to focus on degradation kinetics and water/erosion mechanisms rather than force-field density/Tg validation, and did not surface a citable PCFF- or COMPASS-specific accuracy number in this pass.

findings.claim: A dedicated small-molecule study of urea itself (the exact chemical linkage at the core of every polyurea repeat unit) assesses 4 GAFF-family and 5 OPLS-family force field variants against experimental urea crystal lattice parameters, crystal density, cohesive energy, and aqueous-solution properties. GAFF2 specifically (PURA's actual routed force field) OVER-predicts urea crystal density: calculated 1.476 g/cm3 vs experimental 1.375 g/cm3 (+7.4%). The paper's own text states: 'All force fields slightly underestimate a and overestimate c, and the density, rho, is overestimated by all of the force fields,' i.e. this is a consistent, systematic direction across every GAFF and OPLS variant tested, not GAFF2-specific noise. This study is a small-molecule urea CRYSTAL study -- it does not simulate polyurea (the polymer) at all, and crystal-density errors do not necessarily transfer to amorphous-melt density errors.
findings.title: Assessment of GAFF and OPLS Force Fields for Urea: Crystal and Aqueous Solution Properties
polymers: urea (small molecule, NH2-CO-NH2) -- NOT polyurea; the urea linkage is the repeat-unit-defining functional group shared with PURA's polymer chemistry
findings.reported_errors: Urea crystal density vs experiment (1.375 g/cm3): GAFF1 1.460 (+6.2%), GAFF2 1.476 (+7.4%), GAFF-D1 1.521 (+10.6%), GAFF-D3 1.460 (+6.2%). All force fields tested (GAFF and OPLS families alike) overestimate density; the paper reports 'the experimental form I crystal density [is overestimated] by 7-19%' across the full set.
findings.relevance: The single most directly on-topic finding located for PURA: it is GAFF2 (PURA's actual routed force field), on the exact urea functional group that defines polyurea's repeat unit -- a small-molecule analog in the same spirit as section 6's benzene/toluene benchmark for PS. Important caveat, stated explicitly by the task and preserved here: this is a CRYSTAL density comparison for the monomer compound, not an amorphous bulk-polymer-melt comparison for the polymer -- crystal-packing errors and amorphous-melt errors are not the same quantity and need not share sign or magnitude, so this finding should not be read as a direct GAFF2-polyurea bulk-density prediction.

findings.claim: A 2025 MDPI Polymers paper studies dynamic mechanical properties and energy absorption of what it calls 'polyureas' (PURs) via combined experiment and MD simulation, reporting MD density within 2% of experiment for four variants. However, full-text inspection reveals these are segmented POLYUREA-POLYURETHANE HYBRID elastomers -- built from isophorone diisocyanate (IPDI), diamine chain extenders (D2000, D230), AND macrodiol soft segments (polycarbonate, polycaprolactone, polypropylene glycol, or polytetramethylene ether glycol diols, 'remained at 24 wt%') -- not pure polyurea (urea-linkage-only) chemistry. The force field used is COMPASS, not GAFF or GAFF2: 'The COMPASS force field was chosen for the analog modules Forcite and Amorphous Cell.'
findings.title: Dynamic Mechanical Properties and Energy Absorption Capabilities of Polyureas Through Experiments and Molecular Dynamic Simulation
polymers: segmented polyurea-polyurethane hybrid elastomers (IPDI + D2000/D230 diamine hard segments + 24 wt% polyol/polycarbonate/polycaprolactone/PTMEG diol soft segments) -- NOT pure polyurea
fields: COMPASS (NOT GAFF, NOT GAFF2 -- PURA's actual routed force field)
findings.reported_errors: Density vs experiment, 4 variants: PPG1000-PUR 1.041 MD vs 1.021 exp (+1.9%); PTMG1000-PUR 1.019 vs 1.007 (+1.2%); PCL1000-PUR 1.045 vs 1.051 (-0.6%); PC1000-PUR 1.055 vs 1.053 (+0.2%). Authors state 'these model errors were revealed to be lower than 2%.' Experimental Tg (DMA) range: -48C to -22C.
findings.relevance: FLAGS A DOUBLE SCOPE MISMATCH, not a corroboration: despite being labeled 'polyureas' in the title, this paper is chemically a urea-urethane hybrid segmented elastomer with substantial (24 wt%) diol soft-segment content -- structurally distinct from PURA's pure-urea-linkage chemistry (the class EMC cannot build, routed to RadonPy/GAFF2_mod specifically because of its {na,c_2} amide-N increment gap). It also uses COMPASS, not GAFF2. The strong density accuracy (<2%) reported here therefore cannot be attributed to GAFF2 or to pure polyurea chemistry, and should not be read as evidence for either.

27_pura_gaff2_polyurea_2026_08.synthesis: Both findings are informative but NEITHER directly corroborates NOR contradicts a GAFF2-on-bulk-amorphous-polyurea claim, because none of PURA's own internal density/Tg measurements exist yet to compare against, and neither source combines the correct force field (GAFF2) with the correct chemistry (pure, unblended polyurea) and the correct physical state (bulk amorphous melt) simultaneously. The Anker2023 urea-crystal finding is the closer analog on chemistry and exact force field (GAFF2, urea linkage) but wrong physical state (crystal, not amorphous melt); the Yang2025 'polyurea' finding is the closer analog on physical state (amorphous MD cell, density-vs-experiment reported) but wrong force field (COMPASS, not GAFF2) and wrong chemistry (a urea-urethane hybrid with 24 wt% diol soft segments, not pure polyurea). As anticipated by this task's own framing, and consistent with section 19's already-documented finding that neither of GAFF's founding/update papers contains any polymer validation content at all, this remains -- after a genuine, dedicated search -- a real gap for a GAFF2-specific bulk-amorphous-pure-polyurea density or Tg validation. PURA's own ff_note ('No GAFF2-vs-experiment polyurea literature was located in this session; this remains a genuine open gap') is CORROBORATED and reconfirmed by this search: the gap is real, not merely unsearched, and the two nearest analogs found (urea crystal under GAFF2; urea-urethane hybrid under COMPASS) each close only one of the two axes (force field, chemistry) needed to fill it.

No source combining GAFF2 with pure (non-hybrid) polyurea bulk amorphous-melt density or Tg was located. This is a genuine, actively-searched gap consistent with the existing ff_note's own honest admission and with section 19's independently-established finding that GAFF/GAFF2's own founding and update papers contain zero polymer validation content of any kind.

selection_criteria_extracted.criterion: Prefer a field with a same-polymer or same-family published benchmark reporting signed density/Tg error against experiment, over a field chosen solely on general reputation.
selection_criteria_extracted.how_to_apply: Before adopting a fallback field for a novel/no-experimental-data polymer, search for any same-polymer or same-family multi-FF benchmark (as in the PDMS and PMMA/PIB cases found here); if none exists, treat the fallback choice as unvalidated rather than assuming general-purpose reputation transfers.

selection_criteria_extracted.criterion: Do not assume atom-type/fragment coverage of a novel chemistry by a force field's parameterization set predicts lower simulated-property error; the literature has not established this relationship, and directly measuring it (as we did, -0.26 K, -0.64 density) is more informative than an a-priori coverage argument.
selection_criteria_extracted.how_to_apply: Treat 'this polymer contains atom types outside the field's training set' as a flag for verification-needed, not as a predictor of error direction or magnitude, when deciding whether to trust a force field on a novel polymer.

selection_criteria_extracted.criterion: When no experimental data exists, use CED/solubility-parameter comparison against Hansen/Hildebrand group-contribution tables as an independent (density/Tg-orthogonal) reference-free check, expecting ~1 Hildebrand-unit discriminating accuracy.
selection_criteria_extracted.how_to_apply: Compute CED from the equilibrated MD cell and compare to a group-contribution-estimated solubility parameter for the polymer's chemistry; treat disagreement beyond ~1-2 Hildebrands as a flag against the force field/parameterization, independent of the density/Tg gates already in use.

selection_criteria_extracted.criterion: Group-contribution Tg estimators (van Krevelen/Bicerano-style, or newer hybrid QSPR-GAP) can serve as a reference-free Tg sanity check to roughly 8-10 K or ~5-10% MRE, but only when the polymer's structural fragments are well represented in the estimator's training set; traditional (non-hybrid) group contribution is explicitly reported to degrade on fragments absent from training data.
selection_criteria_extracted.how_to_apply: Use a group-contribution Tg estimate as a secondary sanity bound on simulated Tg for novel polymers, but discount it (do not treat disagreement as force-field evidence) when the polymer's backbone chemistry is not well represented in the estimator's own training set.

selection_criteria_extracted.criterion: A known systematic force-field bias (e.g., a class-wide density deficit) does not by itself justify switching fields; the largest-scale published pipeline (RadonPy) response to an admitted systematic GAFF2 density bias was a statistical/ML post-hoc correction, not a per-chemistry field switch.
selection_criteria_extracted.how_to_apply: If a systematic, well-characterized bias is found (as with our measured -5.9% PCFF density deficit), consider a calibrated post-hoc correction as a literature-precedented alternative to switching to an unvalidated fallback field, especially when the fallback field (e.g. GAFF2 for aromatic backbones) itself lacks chemistry-specific bulk validation.

selection_criteria_extracted.criterion: High-throughput pipelines in the literature fix one force field for an entire cross-chemistry screening campaign rather than performing automated per-polymer force-field selection; there is no published precedent for a per-chemistry FF-selection algorithm to cite or emulate.
selection_criteria_extracted.how_to_apply: Do not present per-polymer automated FF selection as literature-validated methodology; frame it as a novel design choice if implemented, and validate it empirically per family rather than by appeal to precedent.

selection_criteria_extracted.criterion: For an aromatic-ring backbone or pendant group specifically, PCFF/CFF91's own founding validation paper documents a same-family (benzene, toluene) density deficit of -6.3%/-6.5% against experiment, with a mechanistic origin (excess NVT pressure at the true density, i.e. the nonbonded parameters are too repulsive at correct packing) rather than a sampling artifact; COMPASS reduces both compounds' error to -1.1%/-1.2% under identical conditions in the same paper. This is chemistry-matched and mechanism-verified, not a general cross-polymer reputation claim -- it is the strongest single piece of evidence in this document for a specific field switch on a specific chemistry class.
selection_criteria_extracted.how_to_apply: When the repeat unit contains a benzene-like aromatic ring (phenyl pendant, phenylene backbone, etc.) and PCFF is the class default, treat this benzene/toluene benchmark as same-family evidence worth weighing alongside (not instead of) the class's own citations, and consider field_override='compass' as a candidate worth an admissibility check (ff_capability.py) before committing to it -- COMPASS's smaller typing-template vocabulary (96 vs PCFF's 422) means build-time admissibility must be verified per SMILES, it cannot be assumed from this benzene/toluene result. Do NOT extend this reasoning to non-aromatic chemistries -- see the PDMS counter-example above, where COMPASS is the worst of 5 fields tested and errs in the opposite direction.
selection_criteria_extracted.evidence_strength: moderate-to-strong for aromatic chemistries specifically; not applicable outside them

selection_criteria_extracted.criterion: For polymers whose Class-II family member (COMPASS, COMPASS II, PCFF, pcff+) has been benchmarked on the SAME polymer under a DIFFERENT Class-II variant than the class default, treat convergence or divergence between variants as informative: if two different Class-II variants land on nearly the same value for the same polymer (as with PVC bulk modulus: COMPASS 2.9470 GPa vs PolyJarvis's PCFF 2.7-2.9 GPa), that is evidence the effect is Class-II-family-wide rather than specific to the exact variant in use; if they diverge in sign (as with PEEK density: COMPASS II +2.2% over vs PolyJarvis's PCFF -5.1% under), that is evidence the effect is variant- or model-specific and should not be generalized across the Class-II family.
selection_criteria_extracted.how_to_apply: When searching for literature support for a PCFF-routed class, do not restrict the search to 'PCFF' alone -- COMPASS, COMPASS II, and other Class-II variants on the same polymer are informative even though they are not numerically identical to PCFF; report the variant explicitly and read agreement/disagreement in this family-wide-vs-variant-specific frame rather than treating any Class-II result as interchangeable with a PCFF result.

selection_criteria_extracted.criterion: When a literature figure surfaced by a web search summary appears to support a specific target polymer (e.g. 'PLA density error under three force fields'), trace the claim to its actual source paper and confirm what chemistry the number was actually measured on before citing it -- search-engine summarization can silently conflate a cited justification-reference (e.g. a small-molecule n-hexane benchmark used to justify a force-field choice in a PLA paper) with a finding about the target polymer itself.
selection_criteria_extracted.how_to_apply: Before recording any reported_errors figure, verify via WebFetch that the source's OWN abstract/text states the number was measured on the polymer or analog claimed, not merely that the polymer-focused paper CITES a differently-scoped benchmark as justification; when the chemistry doesn't match (e.g. an aliphatic hydrocarbon standing in for an ester-containing polyester), exclude the claim rather than reporting it under the target polymer's name.
selection_criteria_extracted.evidence_strength: strong (this is a documented near-miss caught during this session's own search, not a literature-derived claim)

selection_criteria_extracted.criterion: PCFF/CFF93, OPLS-AA, and TraPPE-UA's own founding papers all validate exclusively against small molecules, model compounds, or short oligomers (up to C12 alkanes for TraPPE-UA) -- none of the three founding papers this codebase's class-routing (server.py _PCFF_CLASSES/_OPLS_CLASSES/_TRAPPE_CLASSES) ultimately rests on contains a bulk amorphous polymer-melt validation of density, Tg, or mechanical properties. This is the SAME pattern section 5 already established for COMPASS (small-molecule/PEO-only founding validation), but for PCFF/CFF93 it is narrower still on the 3 classes where it applies: the paper formally cited as ff_justification_doi on PSTR/PAMD/PSFO (in addition to the on-chemistry PCBN) is specifically a polycarbonate model-compound/crystal-structure derivation (title: 'An ab Initio CFF93 All-Atom Force Field for Polycarbonates') -- an extrapolation from ONE polymer's small-molecule fragments to three compositionally unrelated polymer chemistries, not merely from small molecules to bulk polymers in general. The remaining 11 PCFF-routed classes each cite their own separate DOI and are not affected by this specific mis-citation.
selection_criteria_extracted.how_to_apply: Treat every current class-default force-field citation in polymer_rules.json as validating the FUNCTIONAL FORM and small-molecule parameter-fitting methodology of that force field, not as direct evidence of accuracy on any specific bulk amorphous polymer melt, unless a separate, chemistry-specific downstream paper (of the kind already collected in sections 6-15) is also cited. When routing a genuinely novel polymer to a class default, do not read the class's ff_justification_doi as polymer-melt validation by itself -- search for (or flag the absence of) chemistry-specific downstream literature exactly as sections 6-15 already do per class.

selection_criteria_extracted.criterion: A citation whose TOPIC matches a polymer class (same chemistry family in the title/abstract) can still cite the WRONG FORCE FIELD entirely -- verify the force field actually named and used inside the paper's methods section, not just topical/chemistry match, before recording doi_verified/ff_justification_doi as meaningful support for a PCFF-routed (or any specific-FF-routed) class.
selection_criteria_extracted.how_to_apply: When verifying or searching for a ff_justification_doi, always extract and record the specific force field name used to RUN the simulations (not merely referenced in the background/related-work section), the same way sections 7-15 and this batch (sections 20-27) already do. A chemistry-on-topic paper using a different force field family (e.g. PPHS's cited DOI, on-topic polyphosphazenes but DREIDING, not PCFF) is not evidence for the class's actual routed force field and should be flagged, not treated as validating.
selection_criteria_extracted.evidence_strength: strong (directly demonstrated this round: PPHS's ff_justification_doi, 10.3390/polym14071451, is confirmed via full-text WebFetch to use DREIDING, not PCFF, despite being a topically on-chemistry polyphosphazene paper)

selection_criteria_extracted.criterion: A single MD paper can report multiple, disagreeing Tg (or other property) extraction methods for the same simulated system (e.g. specific-volume-break vs self-diffusion-onset); when transcribing a literature Tg/error figure into ff_note, record which extraction method the number came from, since the paper's own preferred/most-accurate method may differ from the number already circulating in prior notes.
selection_criteria_extracted.how_to_apply: Before transcribing a literature Tg (or density/modulus) figure, check whether the source paper computed it by more than one method and, if so, which method the authors themselves flag as more reliable; prefer that method's number, or record both with their method labels, rather than silently carrying forward whichever number was first transcribed.
selection_criteria_extracted.evidence_strength: moderate (demonstrated this round: Wen2020/PIMN's existing ff_note cites the rho(T)-method Ultem Tg, 525K/+7.1% error, while the same paper's own D(T)-method gives 504K/+2.9% error and is explicitly called more accurate by the paper's own authors)

contradictions_with_our_measurements: In the one same-polymer multi-FF benchmark that included COMPASS directly against other fields (PDMS: COMPASS, OPLS-AA, DREIDING, UA, HUANG), COMPASS was the WORST performer (density RMSE 0.178 g/cm3, largest of the five) and OVER-predicted density, the opposite sign from our measured PCFF under-density deficit. This directly contradicts an assumption that COMPASS would systematically outperform or share PCFF's bias direction on chemistries where PCFF underperforms -- at least for this one polymer.

The PMMA/PIB review reports Class II (PCFF-family) force fields reproducing amorphous density within 2% for both polymers, versus our measured PCFF PMMA deficit of -6.2% -- a roughly 3x discrepancy in magnitude between the literature's reported PCFF-family performance on PMMA and our own measurement, for the same polymer chemistry (though not necessarily the identical PMMA model/tacticity/chain-length/protocol).

GAFF2's only large-scale amorphous-polymer-bulk validation found (RadonPy, >1000 polymers) reports GAFF2 itself has an admitted systematic density bias requiring ML correction -- meaning our fallback-to-GAFF2 assumption (that it is a clean alternative to a biased PCFF) is not supported; GAFF2 has its own known systematic bulk-density bias, just not characterized per-chemistry-family in what we could verify.

No literature source corroborates our specific -5.9% PCFF class-wide magnitude (PEEK -5.3, PEG -5.5, PMMA -6.2, PS -6.5); the one comparable literature case (PMMA/PIB review) reports a much smaller (<2%) Class-II density error for PMMA, suggesting our -6.2% PMMA figure may be protocol-specific (equilibration/annealing/quench-rate dependent) rather than an inherent PCFF limitation -- this is worth cross-checking against our own equilibration protocol before attributing the deficit purely to the force field. UPDATE 2026-08-20, PS specifically: this protocol-vs-FF question was directly tested empirically for PS -- two independent equilibration-time extensions (5->10 anneal cycles; 1ns->10ns melt-phase NPT production, a real run each, not simulated) both converged to -5.94% and -5.85% respectively, essentially unchanged from the original -6.32% and matching the benzene/toluene PCFF benchmark (-6.3%/-6.5%, section 6) closely. For PS specifically this favors the FF-bias explanation over the protocol/kinetics explanation. This does NOT resolve the same question for PMMA/PEEK/PEG, which have not had the equivalent equilibration-time control run.

Our own measured negative correlation between extrapolated-atom-type fraction and |error| (-0.26 K, -0.64 density) has no direct corroboration or contradiction in the literature searched; the closest source (the 82-study review) establishes only that the field has never quantitatively tested this relationship, meaning our finding is not contradicted but is also not independently reproduced elsewhere -- treat it as an internal-archive-specific result until tested on a different polymer set.

PSFO (polysulfone, PCFF): no literature source was found reporting a signed density or Tg error for PCFF or any Class-II variant on polysulfone, polyethersulfone, or a small-molecule diaryl-sulfone/diaryl-ether analog. PolyJarvis's measured -4.0 to -4.3% density deficit and +2-8% Tg offset are therefore NEITHER corroborated NOR contradicted by anything found (2026-08 search) -- this remains a genuine, actively-searched literature gap, consistent with polymer_rules.json's own existing note that no class-specific PCFF validation paper exists for PSFO.

PKTN (PEEK, PCFF): the one directly-on-chemistry literature source found (the same paper as the existing PEEK2020 citation, now re-read for its density figure) reports COMPASS II OVER-predicting PEEK density by +2.2%, the OPPOSITE SIGN from PolyJarvis's measured PCFF PEEK density deficit of -5.1%. Because this compares a different Class-II variant (COMPASS II) on a different structural model (small catechol-based cyclic oligomer, not a full linear amorphous melt), it cannot directly refute the PCFF-specific finding, but it does contradict any assumption that Class-II fields generically under-predict PEEK density -- the sign is evidently variant/model-dependent even within the Class-II family (2026-08 search).

PACR (PMMA, PCFF): re-confirms the pre-existing contradiction already on record (the PMMA/PIB review's <2% Class-II density figure vs our -5.7 to -6.6% measurement) and adds a documented NEGATIVE search result: no literature source was found (2026-08 search) that resolves this 3-4x discrepancy via a tacticity, degree-of-polymerization, or partial-charge-assignment-method mechanism, despite this being the specific, actionable hypothesis Step 2 of this search posed. The discrepancy therefore remains unexplained by anything in the literature searched, not merely under-explained.

PVNL (PVC, PCFF): STRONG NEW CORROBORATION (2026-08 search) of the measured K (bulk modulus) deficit's likely mechanism-class: a full-text-verified COMPASS study of neat PVC reports K = 2.9470 GPa at 298 K via elastic-constant (Reuss) analysis, numerically overlapping PolyJarvis's own PCFF-measured K range of 2.7-2.9 GPa almost exactly. Two different Class-II-family force fields converging on nearly the same (low) K value for the same polymer is evidence that PolyJarvis's ~20-35% K deficit vs its own cited experimental band [3.5,4.5] GPa reflects a Class-II-family-wide characteristic, not a PCFF-specific artifact -- though neither this paper nor any other source found independently confirms that 3.5-4.5 GPa is the correct experimental target (the paper itself makes no density/K vs-experiment claim). PVC Tg (COMPASS +2.7 to +3.2% vs experiment in this same paper) is offered as informative context only, per this task's explicit instruction, since PolyJarvis's own internal PVC Tg fits are judged unreliable and not directly comparable.

PEST (PLA, PCFF): no literature source was found (2026-08 search) reporting a PCFF-specific (as opposed to COMPASS/DREIDING/GAFF) Tg or density error for PLA or a close polyester analog, separable from the already-known multirate-extrapolation-artifact literature this search was instructed to exclude. A superficially relevant PLA/force-field-comparison figure (COMPASS 0.61%/DREIDING 16.16%/PCFF 9.6% density error) was traced to its actual source and found to be an n-hexane (non-ester, non-polyester) small-molecule benchmark cited only as general justification in an unrelated PLA/PPC-composite paper -- NOT a PLA-specific number -- and was excluded rather than misreported. PolyJarvis's own +12.8% PEST Tg offset therefore remains neither corroborated nor contradicted by anything found; the internal single-rate-cooling-artifact attribution stands un-challenged by literature evidence either way.

PHAL (fluoropolymers, opls-aa): a same-family (Viton A, VDF/HFP) multi-force-field comparison (2026-08 search) reports OPLS-derived fields producing systematically too-soft, too-extended-chain, under-packed structures relative to PCFF and experiment -- qualitatively suggesting PHAL's opls-aa default may be prone to UNDER-predicting mechanical stiffness/modulus for PVDF-adjacent chemistries, though no PolyJarvis-internal PHAL bias numbers exist yet to compare against, and no numeric percent-error was recoverable from the paywalled source. This is a new caution, not a new confirmed contradiction.

PSIL (PDMS, opls-aa): no new contradiction or corroboration found this round (2026-08 search only cross-referenced the existing section-1 PDMS 5-force-field benchmark, where OPLS-AA was second-best of five, density RMSE 0.0414 g/cm3) -- this remains PSIL's existing, already-favorable literature support, unchanged.

PHYC (polyolefins, trappe-ua): no new contradiction or corroboration found (2026-08 search) beyond re-confirming the existing Ramos2015 PE citation (Tg=187K vs exp 185-195K, matching); the PP/PIB branched-type Tg-validation gap PHYC's own ff_note already flags as 'medium confidence' remains open and unresolved by this search.

PDIE (polydienes, trappe-ua): no new contradiction or corroboration found (2026-08 search) for TraPPE-UA specifically -- Sharma2016's exact per-force-field numbers remain paywalled and unverified beyond the existing qualitative citation. A chemically-adjacent PCFF-family (pcff+, not TraPPE-UA) cis-1,4-polybutadiene study reporting ~2% density accuracy is encouraging for polydiene MD generally but does not test TraPPE-UA and so cannot corroborate or contradict PDIE's specific field choice.

PCFF founding-paper provenance (4 classes formally cite this DOI, 2026-08-24 search, corrected 2026-08-24): PCFF's ff_justification_doi field is set to Sun 1994 (10.1021/ja00086a030) on exactly 4 classes -- PCBN, PSTR, PAMD, PSFO (independently re-verified against guides/polymer_rules.json directly; the other 11 PCFF-routed classes each cite a different, class-specific DOI of their own). On independent verification, 10.1021/ja00086a030 is titled 'An ab Initio CFF93 All-Atom Force Field for Polycarbonates' -- a polycarbonate-specific model-compound/crystal-structure derivation paper, not a general 'PCFF for polymers' paper. This does not contradict any specific PolyJarvis density/Tg/K NUMBER, but it does contradict the implicit provenance claim for the 3 non-PCBN classes that cite it: by its own title and methodology, it is chemistry-specific to PCBN (polycarbonates) and silent on PSTR/PAMD/PSFO. It does NOT extend to PKTN/PIMD/POXI/PEST/PSUL/PURT/PANH/PPHS/PACR/PIMN/PVNL, which were never formally cited to this DOI in the first place (an earlier draft of this entry incorrectly claimed all 15 PCFF classes were affected; corrected after independently re-checking the polymer_rules.json field values). Sections 6-9 and 11 of this file already document, per-class, that no PCFF-specific bulk validation exists for PS/PMMA/PEEK/PSU/PLA beyond general Class-II reputation -- for PSTR/PAMD/PSFO specifically, this finding supplies part of the explanation for WHY: their cited 'founding' paper was never about their chemistries at all.

PIMD (polyimides/Kapton, PCFF): the formally cited ff_justification_doi (Wen2020, 10.1002/pol.20200050, shared with PIMN) is confirmed via full-text WebFetch to use PCFF explicitly, but covers only BPADA-based aromatic polyetherimides (Ultem-family) -- PMDA-ODA/Kapton, PIMD's own named exemplar chemistry, is never studied in that paper. A second, chemistry-correct source (Rosenauer2024, PMDA-ODA-specific, Young's modulus within the 2.5-3.2 GPa literature range) uses OPLS-AA, not PCFF. Neither source combines the correct force field with the correct chemistry, so PIMD's own PCFF+PMDA-ODA combination remains, after active searching, without any literature validation at all -- consistent with, and reconfirming, PIMD's own ff_note ('no class-specific PCFF MD validation paper available yet'), but revealing that the formal ff_justification_doi field is itself a subfamily scope mismatch (it is really PIMN's citation).

PIMN (polyetherimides/Ultem, PCFF): STRONG CORROBORATION (2026-08-24 search) -- Wen2020 explicitly confirms PCFF ('All MD simulations were performed using LAMMPS with the PCFF force field') and reproduces PIMN's ff_note Tg figure for Ultem almost exactly (525K MD vs 490K exp, +7.1%, matching the note's '+7%'). New nuance: the same paper's own diffusion-based Tg method (504K, +2.9% error) is explicitly called more accurate by its own authors than the specific-volume method already quoted in the note -- worth noting if the ff_note is ever re-transcribed. PIMN's other exemplar chemistry (linear poly(ethylenimine)) remains uncited by this or any other source found.

PPHS (polyphosphazenes, PCFF): STRONG NEW FLAG (2026-08-24 search) -- the formally cited ff_justification_doi (Chen & Demir 2022, 10.3390/polym14071451) is confirmed via full-text WebFetch to use DREIDING, not PCFF or any Class-II force field, despite being topically on-chemistry (polyphosphazenes). It also does not cover the alkoxy/ethoxy substituent chemistry PolyJarvis's own ff_note says is build-tested (it covers Cl- and CF3CH2O-substituted variants instead). This is a new, independently-discovered instance of the force-field-provenance mismatch pattern already documented elsewhere in this file for Sun1994/PCBN (section 16) -- but discovered via a chemistry-on-topic-yet-wrong-FF citation rather than an off-topic citation. A separate source (Sun/Ren/Fried 1998, COMPASS's own phosphazene parameterization paper) confirms a genuine PCFF-to-COMPASS parameter lineage for phosphazene nonbonded terms specifically, supporting the ff_note's separate claim that 'pcff.frc explicitly added polyphosphazene types,' but that validation, too, is small-molecule/crystal-scoped, not bulk-polymer-scoped.

PURT (polyurethanes/TPU, PCFF): NEW FLAG (2026-08-24 search) -- the formally cited ff_justification_doi (10.3390/polym18060679, a real, CrossRef-verified 2026 paper) is confirmed via accessible abstract text to study a CROSSLINKED/CURING thermoset polyurethane network tracked across degree-of-cure via topological crosslinking MD, not PolyJarvis's actual linear/aliphatic TPU melt chemistry -- a physical-system scope mismatch analogous to the Sun1994/PCBN pattern. The specific force field used could not be independently verified through the MDPI paywall; a secondary search-engine summary's claim of 'OPLS-AA/COMPASS/PCFF' could not be corroborated from primary text and is explicitly NOT relied upon here, per this document's established rule (section 11) against trusting unconfirmed search-summarized force-field claims.

PPNL (conjugated/PPV, PCFF): PARTIAL CORROBORATION (2026-08-24 search) -- the Tg figure in PPNL's ff_note (416+/-8K vs exp ~416K) is independently corroborated via CrossRef title/author verification and multiple converging search summaries, and new mechanical-property data (Young's modulus: PA 1.81+/-0.34 GPa, PPV 9.20+/-0.57 GPa) was recovered. However, the specific force-field claim (PCFF) could not be independently re-verified from primary text in this pass -- both Wiley and ResearchGate access attempts returned 403, and no citing-paper methods description was found -- so this remains SILENT (unconfirmed, not contradicted) on the PCFF-identity question specifically. The note's flagged open concern (conjugated-backbone torsional/planarity accuracy) is not addressed by anything found and remains fully open.

PSUL (polythioethers/PPS, PCFF, ff_justification_doi currently null): NEW EVIDENCE, gap partially narrowed but not closed (2026-08-24 search) -- a 2024 Chinese Journal of Polymer Science paper studies PPS directly (PSUL's own exemplar chemistry) as a reference baseline for alkyl-modified variants, confirmed via CrossRef, using COMPASS II (not PCFF) as its primary simulation force field. No quantitative PPS density or Tg vs experiment figure was recoverable from accessible text, only a qualitative Tg/modulus trend across the alkyl-substituted series. This is the first on-chemistry Class-II-family PSUL/PPS source documented in this file, but it does not supply a PCFF-specific or even a fully quantitative accuracy number, so the gap PSUL's own ff_note already documents ('No PCFF-vs-experiment polythioether/PPS literature was located') remains substantively open.

PANH (polyanhydrides, PCFF, ff_justification_doi currently null): GAP RECONFIRMED as genuine after active search (2026-08-24) -- no PCFF, COMPASS, or Class-II-family density/Tg validation for poly(sebacic anhydride), any other polyanhydride, or a close small-molecule anhydride analog was located. One candidate (a small-molecule succinic-anhydride crystal/melting study, DOI 10.1002/1521-3765(20020402)8:7<1710::AID-CHEM1710>3.0.CO;2-A, CrossRef-verified) was traced and excluded because it uses a custom organic-crystal-adapted force field (not PCFF/Class-II) and studies crystal melting rather than bulk amorphous-liquid density -- the same exclusion logic already applied to the n-hexane paper nearly misattributed to PEST in section 11. This confirms, rather than merely repeats, PANH's own ff_note admission that no such literature exists.

PURA (polyureas, GAFF2_mod, ff_justification_doi currently null): TWO PARTIAL, NON-OVERLAPPING ANALOGS FOUND, gap reconfirmed as genuine for the full GAFF2+pure-polyurea+bulk-amorphous combination (2026-08-24 search). (1) A small-molecule urea-crystal force-field assessment (Anker2023, DOI 10.1021/acs.cgd.3c00785, CrossRef-verified) reports GAFF2 OVER-predicting urea crystal density by +7.4% (1.476 vs 1.375 g/cm3) -- correct force field (GAFF2) and correct linkage chemistry (urea), but wrong physical state (crystal, not amorphous melt); this is informative context, not a direct bulk-density prediction, and should not be assumed to share sign/magnitude with an amorphous-melt error. (2) A 2025 paper titled around 'polyureas' (Yang2025, DOI 10.3390/polym17010107, CrossRef-verified) reports <2% MD-vs-experiment density error for what full-text inspection reveals are actually segmented polyurea-polyurethane HYBRID elastomers (24 wt% diol soft segments) simulated with COMPASS, not GAFF2 -- correct physical state (amorphous MD cell with a density comparison) but wrong force field and wrong (hybrid, not pure) chemistry. Neither source closes the gap PURA's own ff_note already documents, and this reconfirms section 19's independent finding that GAFF/GAFF2's own founding and update papers contain zero polymer validation content.
overall_confidence: Moderate on general selection-methodology conclusions (high-throughput pipelines fix one field per campaign; transferability-predicts-error is unestablished in the literature; CED is an established but underused reference-free check) -- unchanged by the 2026-08 (sections 7-15) search round. For PS specifically, confidence remains moderate-to-high (from section 6, 2026-08-20) that its -5.9%-ish PCFF density deficit is a genuine aromatic-ring limitation rather than an equilibration-protocol gap, via the mechanism-verified benzene/toluene benchmark from PCFF's own founding paper plus two independent real equilibration-time-extension runs that failed to close the gap; this conclusion remains chemistry-specific (aromatic rings) and is not generalized to other classes without their own equivalent check. Chemistry-specific coverage is now widened across 9 additional classes (sections 7-15) but remains UNEVEN, and confidence must be read per-class, not as a single number: (1) SOLID literature backing pre-existed and is reconfirmed for PSIL/PDMS (favorable, same-polymer, 5-FF benchmark, OPLS-AA second-best of five). (2) STRENGTHENED this round: PVNL/PVC's bulk-modulus deficit now has same-polymer, cross-Class-II-variant corroboration (COMPASS K=2.95 GPa closely matching PolyJarvis's own PCFF K=2.7-2.9 GPa) -- this is the strongest new finding of this search round, though it lacks an independent experimental K reference from the source paper itself, so it corroborates a MECHANISM (Class-II-family-wide K underestimate) more than it confirms an absolute error magnitude against experiment. (3) MIXED/CONTRADICTED this round: PKTN/PEEK's new COMPASS-II finding (+2.2% density OVER-prediction) is opposite-signed from PolyJarvis's own PCFF -5.1% deficit, adding nuance (Class-II variant/model-dependence) rather than resolving the discrepancy; PACR/PMMA's pre-existing <2%-vs-(-5.7 to -6.6%) discrepancy remains fully unexplained after a dedicated, unsuccessful search for a tacticity/DP/charge-method mechanism. (4) STILL GENUINELY OPEN, confirmed as gaps rather than assumptions after active searching this round: PSFO (polysulfone) and PEST (PLA) have NO chemistry-specific PCFF density/Tg literature at all, same-polymer or analog -- this matches the pre-existing pattern already documented for PEEK/PEG/PMMA/PS density-magnitude coverage in sections 1-5; PHYC's PP/PIB branch-type Tg gap and PDIE's exact TraPPE-UA numeric-accuracy gap (paywall-blocked, qualitative-only) also remain open. (5) NEW CAUTION, not yet a confirmed bias: PHAL's opls-aa default has a same-family (Viton A) qualitative signal of under-predicting fluoropolymer mechanical stiffness relative to PCFF, worth watching in future PHAL runs but not yet quantified since no PolyJarvis-internal PHAL bias numbers exist yet and no numeric literature error was recoverable through the paywall.
